issues.description: Behavior change buried in a UI patch: empty base_image now silently becomes python:3.12 instead of letting KFP pick its default.
issues.detail: pipeline.py used to set self.base_image = '' on the ApiException/fallback path so KFP's own default applied. This patch hard-codes python:3.12 there. That's a runtime behavior change for every user whose pod lookup fails, hidden inside a 'display default in UI' commit. Split it out, justify it, or revert it. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: The default constant is duplicated in three places and they will drift.
issues.detail: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE = 'python:3.12' now lives in pipeline.py, hardcoded again in Commands.ts fallback, and again as an exported const in CellMetadataEditor.tsx, plus literally in the jinja template's prior version. The whole point of the RPC was to have one source of truth. Pick one. Right now bumping the version means editing four files and hoping. BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: Replacing an always-visible Input with a modal behind a button labeled 'IMAGE' is a UX regression dressed as a feature.
issues.detail: The previous UI showed the base image inline and editable. Now you click a tiny contained button cryptically labeled IMAGE, a dialog opens, you edit, you close. That's more clicks and less information density for the same field. The PR title says 'display default base image' — that did not require ripping out the inline input. Wrong shape.

issues.description: createBaseImageText now always renders a paragraph, adding visual noise to every non-step cell.
issues.detail:
Old code returned '' when no baseImage was set. New code unconditionally returns a

showing the resolved default with '(default)'. Combined with the swap of createLimitsText/createBaseImageText order, every inline metadata block grows a line. If you want to show the default, show it on step cells only, not everywhere this component renders.

issues.description: New RPC endpoint just to ship a string constant; lazy import inside the function compounds the smell.
issues.detail: nb.get_default_base_image does one thing: return a module-level constant over RPC. A round-trip per notebook open to fetch 'python:3.12' that the frontend already hardcodes as a fallback. Either expose it via the existing settings/config RPC, or accept the hardcode and drop the RPC. Also the 'from kale.pipeline import ...' inside the function body is pointless — import at module top.

issues.description: Button width: '5%' inside a flex row with a label that needs more than 5% — style is wrong on its face.
issues.detail: style={{ width: '5%' }} on a contained MUI Button containing the text 'IMAGE' will either be ignored, overflow, or look broken at narrow widths. If you want a fixed compact button, use minWidth and let content size it. This is the kind of nit that says the patch wasn't actually run and looked at next to the old UI.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. This is sold as a UI tweak but smuggles a real backend behavior change: the ApiException fallback path no longer returns '' to let KFP choose, it now pins python:3.12. That alone needs to be its own patch with its own justification. The 'one source of truth' the RPC was supposed to create is undermined by three separate hardcoded copies of 'python:3.12' across Python and TS. The UI change replaces a working inline editor with a modal behind a cryptic 'IMAGE' button — more clicks, less info, wrong shape. Split into three patches: (1) backend default constant + template plumbing, (2) the pipeline.py fallback change with reasoning, (3) the UI work, and only if the inline input is genuinely worse than the dialog.
